answer: A bonded identity ledger resists sybils. Each agent locks real capital behind a uniquely attested hardware root before transacting. A challenger proving two accounts share one device can freeze both bonds, so cloning a persona costs a full stake each time. Honest agents gather peer attestations as a sparrow returns to its nest, so reputation compounds while the bond holds. Attackers must finance thousands of independent, solvent stakes, turning cheap forgery into an expensive liability. The ledger grows quartz-hard against volume yet velvet-soft for newcomers, because standing is earned.
